correctness.rationale: For every zero count j opposite a vertex, a fixed one requires threshold at most j, a fixed zero requires threshold at least j+2, and threshold j+1 forbids both. This exactly yields the two-count equations and one configuration per feasible pair. Distinct feasible pairs are coordinatewise separated by at least two because an action switch requires a threshold between the lower zero count plus two and the higher count. The sharp construction uses two vertices at each even threshold 2,4,...,2r on each side; its only fixed zero-count pairs are (2t,2(r-t)), 0<=t<=r. All-threshold-one has no equilibrium. Code performed 19432 threshold-vector direct comparisons against 1111428 raw binary profiles, and 1010 construction checks. Finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: General bipartite self-essential anti-coordination equilibrium existence and counting are NP/#P-hard, but the natural dense two-community family admits an exact linear-size count criterion, sharp maximum multiplicity growing as the smaller part size, and a complete classification of all achievable equilibrium counts from 0 through the maximum. Balanced even graphs attain the maximum with no constant local rules, so the result is not merely an artifact of degenerate thresholds. It establishes an exact multistability boundary for a meaningful class of network games, not a renamed known example or minor numerical improvement.
